note: Narration for the Showtime walkthrough. `durationMs` is the slot reserved for the clip: scripts/showtime-render.mjs fails if a rendered clip is longer. `full: true` lines are only used by `--full`. Persona voices come from src/shared/personas.ts (voiceName); edit text here and run `npm run showtime:render`. `{name}` is replaced with the speaking persona's displayName from src/shared/personas.ts.

lines.text: Hello, I'm {name}, an AI helper. Last time you needed one hint. Shall we call Lily?
You can say my name, press a shortcut, or press a button. I only listen when you ask me to.
I'll show you each step, and you do it. First, the camera icon.
After every step I look again, and a tick means it worked.
Press the green Start call button.
Then the blue Join, not the small one at the top.
That small Join up here is a different button. Ignore it; the ring shows the right one.
You did it. I drew the way, and you clicked.
Two clean steps, so I step back. Watch the chip.
Now you start the call. I'll stay quiet.
Look for the big green button under Lily's name.
Fewer hints each time. That's the number that matters.
If you get stuck, I help a little more, then fade again. A person decides that, not a guess.
A text has just arrived. Let me check it for you.
Three warning signs: it rushes you, it threatens you, and the web address is odd.
I can't be sure, so please ring the number on your bank card.
Three quick specialists read the link, the wording and the sender. A stronger model weighs them and writes the answer.
I never call a message safe. I tell you what looks wrong, and who to ask.
Hello, I'm {name}. A different voice, the same rules: I teach, and you stay in control.
Pick whichever of us you find easier to listen to. Your profile follows you.
That's not a lesson I had saved, so I work it out from your screen.
Click the microphone button here.
Muted. One step, one ring. Ask me about anything on your screen.
I can open it for you, or show you how. It's your choice.
Done. I opened it, and it's written in your log. Next time I can show you how.
I never pay, send, delete or sign in for you. Those stay yours.
It's in Documents, Health: your GP letter from Riverside Surgery.
I only look in folders you chose, and I only read. Nothing leaves your computer for that.
You choose how I look: glass, a dyslexia-friendly font, bigger text.
And I only remember what you let me. Watch, I'll forget this line.
Stop is always on screen. One press ends everything.
The screen is read only while we are talking, and nothing is stored except this file.
Here is what you can do now, and your hints per task. They're going down.
That's the goal: you need me less each week. Now it's your turn. Ask me anything.
Behind the ring, a Gemini model finds the button on your real screen, and checks the result with a fresh look.
The level is decided by plain code, not by the model. Clean tries move it up, stalls move it down.
For anything unplanned, Gemini Argon plans the steps from your screen, and the first step is checked before I point.
Typing works the same way. The voice goes quiet, and my answers appear as chat.
Every attempt is saved in a plain file you own. You can read it, edit it, or delete it.
